rationale_overall: This week's pool is dominated by non-investable noise: routine SpaceX/ISS crew-rotation and splashdown stories (no new financial catalyst), Zaporizhzhia plant shelling and Russia's missile-treaty withdrawal (geopolitical risk, not a tradeable equity catalyst), a Boeing fighter-jet labor strike (negative, not thesis-relevant to any held name), and scattered small-cap/robotics-competition/local-news filler. The one candidate with real financial substance -- Rocket Lab (RKLB) beating Q2 estimates and guiding to a 'record year' -- is undercut by its own coverage framing ('after soaring 800% in 12 months, is RKLB still a buy?'), which reads as a maturing/peak-enthusiasm signal rather than an early-buildup entry point, and NuScale's SMR project trouble is an outright negative for the nuclear wave rather than a reason to add. Denison's uranium results and the AI-chip/data-center items (Samsung-Tesla, Alibaba, GPT-5) are single-article, non-catalytic mentions with no dated evidence of a durable inflection. Nothing here breaches the thesis for AAPL, GOOGL, MSFT, or NVDA, and no rising-wave vehicle clears the bar for a swap this week. Holding the current watchlist unchanged.
